notes: Identity independently checked: supplied canonical text is a six-page primary research article-in-press, titled Mortality salience and morality: Thinking about death makes people less utilitarian, by Bastien Trémolière, Wim De Neys, and Jean-François Bonnefon. DOI 10.1016/j.cognition.2012.05.011 appears in the article footer and matches the reference. Pagination is the supplied in-press pagination, not final journal pages. No PDF was supplied. No study, outcome, sample, or specific test identifies the intended effect beyond p. 3. Candidates in Experiment 1: problem-type main effect F(1,83)=87.46, p<.001, effect-size string g2p=.51 in canonical text; interaction F(1,83)=6.89, p=.01, g2p=.08; conflict simple comparison t(83)=3.03, p=.003; control simple comparison t(83)=1.04, p=.30. These are candidate observations only, not assigned values. The canonical text renders the ANOVA effect-size symbol as g2p; requested Cohen's f^2 is not established and no conversion or symbol repair was performed. Experiment 1 method gives 85 recruited participants; this is retained only as a candidate contributor/recruitment count because target correspondence and explicit critical-model analytic N are unresolved. The 58 independent pretest participants and 115 Experiment 2 participants are not combined. No arithmetic derivation. Original status done means all assigned fields were examined, not that a unique target was resolved. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
